content.title: About
content.content: Pioppini (Agrocybe aegerita) are small forest mushrooms that commonly grow under oak trees in Europe and Asia. They have a delicate nutty aroma, light‑brown color and a slightly crisp texture. Pioppini are widely used as a flavorful ingredient in sauces, risottos, pastas and soups.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pioppini are called “oak mushrooms” because they often form a mycorrhizal relationship with oak roots.
In Japan they are known as “enokita” and feature in traditional dishes.
The mushrooms are rich in B‑vitamins, especially niacin and riboflavin.
Dried pioppini can be stored for up to a year while retaining their aroma and taste.
Culinary practice often calls for a quick sauté until golden to release their nutty scent.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamins B1, B2 and B3 support energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: Dry mushrooms contain about 250 kcal per 100 g, making them a good addition to calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Antioxidant compounds
items.content: Polyphenols and ergothioneine in the mushrooms help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Beta‑glucans stimulate the activity of immune cells.

items.title: Mushroom allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to mushrooms, ranging from skin rash to respiratory symptoms.

items.title: Purine content
items.content: Mushrooms contain purines, so people with gout should limit their intake.

items.title: Toxicity from improper storage
items.content: Freshly harvested mushrooms can spoil quickly; discard them if they develop an off‑odor.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pioppini can be used fresh or dried. Dried mushrooms are re‑hydrated in warm water, then sautéed with garlic and olive oil. They are added to risotto, pasta, sauces, soups and casseroles. Fresh mushrooms are ideal for quick pan‑frying or braising.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dried pioppini in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. Fresh mushrooms should be used within 1‑2 days and kept in the refrigerator in a paper bag to avoid excess moisture.
